title: Rotate Three Values
statement:
Rotate three values one place to the left: `a` gets the value of `b`, `b` gets the value of `c`, and `c` gets the old value of `a`. Use a single assignment when your language allows it.

The input is one line with three integers `a`, `b`, and `c`, each between -1000000 and 1000000, separated by spaces. After the rotation, print `a`, `b`, and `c` on one line, separated by single spaces. Some or all of the numbers can be equal, and they can be zero or negative.

Input:

```text
1 2 3
```

Expected output:

```text
2 3 1
```
hints: If you assign one at a time, the old value of `a` is gone by the time `c` needs it.
Assign all three at once, or save the old `a` in a temporary variable first.

python.solution:
def rotate_left(a: int, b: int, c: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    a, b, c = b, c, a
    return a, b, c


a, b, c = map(int, input().split())
a, b, c = rotate_left(a, b, c)
print(a, b, c)
